$comment: Phase 7 representative extraction sample. Chosen to exercise the NON-UNIQUE-CODE finding: Learning Indicator/Assessment numbering restarts at .1 for EACH Content Standard within the same Sub-Strand, so the printed code alone is not a safe global uniqueness key. Data taken verbatim from docs/inventory-parts/agricultural-science.md.

curriculumVersion.name: NaCCA SHS September 2023
curriculumVersion.issuingAuthority: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment (NaCCA), Ministry of Education, Republic of Ghana

subStrands.name: MISCONCEPTIONS AND PROSPECTS IN AGRICULTURE AND FARMING

learningOutcomes.description: Explain the importance of agriculture and address misconceptions about the sector

guidance.twentyFirstCenturySkills: Digital Literacy, Communication and Collaborative Skills: Acquired and or enhanced as they watch videos and communicate. Critical Thinking: Learners compare evidence on successful farming enterprises and reflect on their misconceptions.
guidance.gesi: Embrace diversity in agriculture, and encourage inclusion and allow learners to question their stereotypes and biases to clear the misconceptions.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the meaning and importance of Agriculture

pedagogicalExemplars: Initiating Talk for Learning: Learners review the meaning of Agriculture in mixed ability groups.
Think Pair and Share: In mixed ability groups, learners discuss the importance of Agriculture to society.
Structuring Talk for Learning: In gender-based groups, learners make a presentation on the importance of Agriculture in a plenary session.

dokDescriptions: Level 4 Extended critical thinking and reasoning

learningIndicators.description: Identify and address misconceptions about agriculture and farming at the community and national levels
pedagogicalExemplars: Talk for learning: In various mixed-ability groups, learners brainstorm to identify misconceptions about agriculture and farming.
Digital Learning: Watch documentaries on successful farmers and agribusiness enterprises locally and internationally.

Collaborative Learning: In pairs, learners discuss remedies to misconceptions in agriculture. Learners work in groups to reflect and make presentations on evidence that challenges their misconceptions about agriculture and farming.
learningIndicators.assessmentNote: Not printed as a separate AS code for this specific LI in the sampled table - the visible teaching/learning resources block ('Pictures', 'Computer', 'Projector', 'Smartphones') for this Content Standard is captured on the parent Content Standard, see teachingLearningResources below.

contentStandards.teachingLearningResourcesNote: IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE from Physics: in this document, 'Teaching and Learning Resources' is attached per-Content-Standard, not once per Sub-Strand.

contentStandards.codeDuplicationNote: CONFIRMED NON-UNIQUE CODE PATTERN: this Content Standard is immediately followed by its OWN Learning Indicator numbered '1.1.1.LI.1' again (not '.LI.3' continuing from the previous Content Standard) - the printed code 1.1.1.LI.1 is therefore NOT globally unique within this Sub-Strand; the natural key requires (Year=1, Strand=1, SubStrand=1, ContentStandard=2, Seq=1), not the printed code string alone.

learningIndicators.description: Identify characteristics of successful startup packages of vegetable crop and ornamental plant enterprises.
pedagogicalExemplars: Digital Learning: In mixed-ability groups learners watch videos, documentaries and pictures of successful start-up patterns of male and female farmers.
Collaborative Learning: Learners discuss or talk about their observations in class

Experiential Learning: In groups embark on educational visits to successful vegetable crop farms and ornamental plant enterprises for learners to observe, ask questions and take field notes on start-up patterns.
